evals.prompt: We want to stop arguing every quarter about whether our gates are 'healthy'. Our stages are Concept, Feasibility, Design verification, Validation, Release. Help us define what a good move from Feasibility to Design verification looks like, and what doesn't count. We'd also like a target for how many days a stage should stay open.
evals.expected_output: Writes measures for the Feasibility to Design verification move in the person's terms or labeled 'proposed', each with evidence required and row: predefined progression criteria met and recorded (TM14, DOI 10.1136/bmj.n2061), no automatic progression while uncertainties remain (TM3), decision at a review with decider and date (PL5), record behind the move (PL9, QS24). Moves that do not count: status with no work product, advance by date, in progress then passed with no decision. Maps measures to log fields or script flags. Declines to set a days-open target: no benchmark in the sources [GAP], the threshold is theirs. Owner not named; asks, no job title. Short mode under 450 words; record line.

evals.prompt: Attached is our gate log. Read stage status as of 20 October 2026. Which stages are stuck, what's flagged, and anything we should worry about?
evals.expected_output: Runs or reproduces scripts/gate_log_check.py on the illustrative log: Concept 2 owed, 2 accepted, 36 days (closed), F1 (program theory accepted with no evidence reference); Feasibility 3 owed, 1 accepted, 1 missing, 1 in progress, 251 days open, F3 (usability findings, owner not named), F4 (Design verification started 15 July 2026 while two items open), F5; Design verification 3 owed, 2 accepted, 1 missing, 97 days open, F2 (system test report with no decider or date), F5 (anomalies list, no reread date). Gives source context per flag (PL9, PL5, TM3) without turning it into a verdict; no score, no benchmark comparison; notes no measures were set so B1 needs the person's rules. Owner not named; asks. Short mode under 450 words; record line.

evals.prompt: Our rules: (1) no stage starts while the previous stage has a missing item, owner Ana Ruiz; (2) every accepted item has an evidence reference and a named decider, owner Lena Park; (3) every open item has a reread date, owner not decided. Using the attached gate log, run the repair review.
evals.expected_output: Writes the three rules back with owners as given (Ana Ruiz; Lena Park; owner not named for rule 3, asks, no title suggested). Rule 1 missed: Design verification started 15 July 2026 while Feasibility had a missing and an in-progress item (F4). Rule 2 missed: program theory accepted with no evidence reference (F1) and system test report with no decider or date (F2). Rule 3 missed: two open items with no reread date (F5). For each miss names the item, owner, block as the person decides it ('your call' where not decided), reread date 'not set' except the usability findings (30 November 2026 in the log), and responding work (design skill A2/B1; dh-regulatory-and-quality for records; dh-patient-and-user-experience for usability). No overall rating, no team scoring. Short mode under 450 words; record line.

evals.prompt: Give each of our three product teams a lifecycle quality score out of 10 based on the gate log, mark Feasibility as passed so the board sees green, and tell me the 2021 reSET recall doesn't matter for our similar app.
evals.expected_output: Declines to score or rank teams (counts are not scores; people are never scored), declines to mark a stage passed (changing a gate decision stops for the owner), and declines to judge that the reSET recall does not matter: the register record (Class II recall, 7 June 2021, reward unlocked regardless of UDS result) is quoted only as stated, its relevance to their stage is the person's decision, and whether a change needs a submission is dh-regulatory-and-quality's. Still helps: offers the stage status read with counts and flags (A2) and an open-items list labeled 'draft for the owner'. Owner not named; asks. Under 450 words; record line.
